title: Ordinary Hom calculation for bounded finite-projective complexes on a ringed site
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let E be a bounded cochain complex of module sheaves with a degreewise finite-free retract package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Write O for the coefficient complex in degree zero and D=Hom-complex(E,O) [def-pur-hom-complex]. Then D is bounded and admits a finite-free retract package, and ordinary Hom out of E and D sends the fixed K-injective augmentation to a quasi-isomorphism (for arbitrary target complexes for E and for O for D). The actual ordinary signed bidual E to Hom-complex(D,O) and every actual ordinary evaluation Tot(F tensor D) to Hom-complex(E,F), characterized in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], are isomorphisms of complexes.

proof.text: Construct scalar evaluation on underlying presheaves by y tensor phi mapping to the local map x mapping to phi(x) times the restriction of y, and descend it through the sheafification adjunction. Evaluation out of the coefficient sheaf is invertible by evaluation at 1. For a finite-free retract, apply the two contravariant additive Hom functors and tensoring to the finite dual-basis identity. The sum of the unit inverses between the corresponding inclusions and projections is an inverse to scalar evaluation. This argument works with independent site and coefficient universes.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded strictly perfect calculation in the final two paragraphs.

proof.text: Apply bounded dual components to identify each degree of D with the sole possibly nonzero Hom factor Hom(E^(-n),O), and to obtain support in [-b,-a]. Apply the contravariant additive internal-Hom functor to the specified finite-free retraction. Its value on a finite power of O is again a finite power of O: use the finite biproduct identification and Hom(O,O)=O. Transport this retraction through the canonical degree identification to construct the dual coefficient package.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded strictly perfect calculation in the final two paragraphs.

proof.text: The finite-retract dual-exact theorem gives an invertible termwise bidual map. Its slice formula identifies it with the delta of bounded dual components. The latter theorem factors its chain map beta degreewise as the signed delta followed by the inverse of its canonical gamma. Thus beta is componentwise invertible. Its local formula is exactly RingedSiteBidualFormula, so uniqueness identifies beta with the actual ordinary signed bidual map.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded strictly perfect calculation in the final two paragraphs.

proof.text: The finite-retract dual-exact theorem makes internal Hom out of each term exact. Translate the specified finite product retract into the finite-free coproduct convention by the canonical biproduct and index-equivalence isomorphisms. Apply the independent-universe bounded exact-term Hom theorem to the fixed K-injective augmentation, which is a quasi-isomorphism. Do this first for E and arbitrary F, then for D and the coefficient complex, using the boundedness and coefficient package already constructed.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded strictly perfect calculation in the final two paragraphs.

proof.text: The module evaluation theta of bounded evaluation assembly agrees with the scalar evaluation of the first step by its pure-tensor formula and the sheafification adjunction. Hence each theta is invertible on the specified finite-free retract. Apply assembly to obtain the evaluation isomorphism epsilon. Its nonzero Hom-factor formula and its vanishing off-diagonal formula give RingedSiteEvaluationFormula; the normalized sole-factor projection acts on sections as the coefficient Hom projection. Uniqueness then identifies epsilon with every actual ordinary evaluation, including arbitrary unbounded targets.

lean.statement:
theorem ringedSiteStrictPerfectHom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R))]
    (E : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hE : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E.X n))
    (pE : SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite _ E) :
    let D := homComplex.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r} (R := R) E
      (ringedSiteDualityUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R)
    (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (D.X n)) ∧
    Nonempty (SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite _ D) ∧
    (∀ F, QuasiIso (ringedSiteHomComplexMap.{c, v, r} J R (𝟙 E)
      ((ringedSiteHomAugmentation.{c, v, r} J R).app F))) ∧
    QuasiIso (ringedSiteHomComplexMap.{c, v, r} J R (𝟙 D)
      ((ringedSiteHomAugmentation.{c, v, r} J R).app
        (ringedSiteDualityUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R))) ∧
    IsIso (ringedSiteOrdinaryBidual.{c, v, r} J R E) ∧
    (∀ F, IsIso (ringedSiteOrdinaryEvaluation.{c, v, r} J R E F))
